transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today; what brings you in to see me?

For years now I’ve felt this constant heaviness and sadness that never really lifts, even when things in my life are going okay. It just feels like I'm carrying a quiet, heavy weight around with me all the time, and I've finally realized I can't keep trying to manage it on my own.
During these years of feeling this way, have you ever had a period of two months or longer where you felt completely back to your normal self?

No, not at all. Over these last three years, there hasn't been a single period—let alone two months—where this heaviness lifted and I felt like my old self. It has just been a continuous, steady weight that never really gives me a break.
Has this feeling of heaviness remained at a steady, milder level throughout these three years, or have there been times when it became much more severe and deeply affected your ability to function?

It has definitely not been mild; it's a severe, constant heaviness that has deeply impacted my ability to function. I've gone from being active and outgoing to turning down social invitations and avoiding high-profile projects at work because I simply don't have the energy to engage with life anymore.
Before this current three-year period of constant heaviness, did you ever experience another distinct period in your life where you felt severely depressed for at least a few weeks or months?

I don't recall experiencing any prior distinct periods of severe depression before these last three years. However, in the years leading up to this, I was dealing with a lot of gradual emotional distance and stress in my marriage before we finally separated.
Along with the low energy, have you also experienced intense feelings of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or thoughts of death or self-harm during these past three years?

I constantly feel like a failure, especially because of my failed marriage, and I feel like an imposter at work who is just pretending to keep up. Whenever anything goes wrong, I immediately blame myself and feel like I'm simply not good enough at anything. However, I have never had any thoughts of death or self-harm.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite during these past three years?

My sleep has been deeply affected; I lie in bed exhausted but wired, and then wake up at three or four in the morning with my mind spinning about work and the divorce, leaving me feeling completely unrested. My appetite, however, has remained relatively normal and hasn't really been a major issue.
Thinking back to when this three-year period of sadness began, did it seem to develop very gradually over a long period, or did it come on relatively quickly over a few weeks?

It was really a mix of both. There was a gradual buildup of stress and emotional distance in my marriage over several years, but this constant, heavy sadness really solidified and deepened around the time of our separation about three years ago.
Have you ever had a period of a few days or more where you felt unusually energetic, hyperactive, or 'on top of the world,' needing much less sleep than usual?

No, I have never experienced anything like that at all. My mood has been consistently heavy and low, without any of those kinds of highs or bursts of energy. It has just been a steady, exhausting weight.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a continuous, severe depressive state lasting for three years, characterized by depressed mood, significantly reduced energy, loss of interest in social and professional activities, disturbed sleep (insomnia), and marked feelings of worthlessness and guilt. Although the chronic three-year duration could suggest dysthymia (F34.1), the high severity of the symptoms and the profound functional impairment align more accurately with a prolonged single depressive episode (F32).
